findings.checklist_item: - [ ] For each of the 14 inbound and 14 outbound mutation types, specify a concrete verification oracle (e.g., which local store field or DC REST response field is read, and what value is asserted) — not just that it is 'asserted individually'.
evidence: 'each asserted individually rather than by an aggregate converged line' — the HOW is never specified
Only the inbound create case has a named oracle: '_jira_key_to_local_id(remote_key) AND asserts the binding store'
No transport method, local-store field path, or DC REST endpoint is named for verifying any of the other 26 mutations
findings.finding: For 13 of the 14 inbound mutations and 13 of the 14 outbound mutations, no verification oracle is specified. The plan says 'each asserted individually rather than by an aggregate converged line' but gives no proving command or observable for any mutation other than inbound create (which has a prior CI run as evidence). An executor must invent verification strategies for 'edit summary', 'add label', 'transition status', 'create link', 'delete issue', etc.
findings.location: Section 'The DC-side mutation suite'; AC 'every mutation in the suite above round-trips, each asserted individually'
scenarios: Executor writes a single 'no exception' assertion for each mutation and calls it 'individual assertion', satisfying the letter but not the spirit
A mutation silently no-ops (the swallowed-exception pattern the plan itself documents for set_parent) and passes a vacuous check

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Amend the 'every mutation round-trips' AC to explicitly exclude `set_parent`'s epic case and instead cite the `pytest.raises(NotImplementedError)` direct-transport assertion as its verification, so the two sections are consistent.
evidence: Plan body: 'set_parent's epic case is expected to raise NotImplementedError ... asserted DIRECTLY AGAINST THE TRANSPORT (with pytest.raises(NotImplementedError): transport.set_parent(...)), NOT through the reconciler subprocess'
AC text: 'every mutation in the suite above round-trips, each asserted individually rather than by an aggregate converged line'
The 14-mutation outbound list includes 'set parent' with no exclusion noted in the AC
findings.finding: The plan body explicitly states that `set_parent`'s epic case raises `NotImplementedError` and must be asserted DIRECTLY AGAINST THE TRANSPORT via `pytest.raises`, NOT through the reconciler (because the exception is swallowed by `dispatch_one._update_one_apply_parent`). Yet the AC 'every mutation in the suite above round-trips, each asserted individually' covers all 14 outbound mutations without carving out set_parent. An implementer reading the AC literally would either (a) attempt a round-trip that the plan body says is impossible and the transport will refuse, or (b) exclude set_parent from the round-trip AC and silently under-deliver against the literal criterion text. The two sections send the implementer in opposite directions.
findings.location: Approach section ('The DC-side mutation suite', outbound set_parent bullet) vs. AC 'every mutation in the suite above round-trips, each asserted individually'
scenarios: Implementer writes a round-trip test for set_parent and it fails because NotImplementedError is expected, or they exclude it and the AC is under-covered.
A reviewer checking the AC against the test suite finds set_parent is tested differently from every other mutation, with no AC language permitting this divergence.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'every mutation in the suite above round-trips, each asserted individually' with 'every mutation in the suite above round-trips individually, EXCEPT set_parent's epic case, which is asserted via `pytest.raises(NotImplementedError)` directly against the transport (not the reconciler subprocess).'

findings.finding: The AC 'every mutation in the suite above round-trips, each asserted individually' is contradicted by the body's explicit carve-out that `set_parent`'s NotImplementedError MUST be asserted 'directly against the transport... NOT through the reconciler subprocess'. 'Round-trips' implies a full reconciler pass; the body forbids exactly that for `set_parent`. An implementer reading only the AC would route `set_parent` through the subprocess (where the exception is swallowed, making the test vacuous), while an implementer reading the body would not. The AC must explicitly exclude `set_parent` from the 'round-trips' clause and state the transport-direct assertion method instead.
findings.location: AC: 'every mutation in the suite above round-trips, each asserted individually' vs. body section 'The DC-side mutation suite' — outbound set_parent paragraph
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'every mutation in the suite above round-trips, each asserted individually' with: 'every mutation in the suite above round-trips and is asserted individually — except `set_parent`, which is asserted directly against the transport via `pytest.raises(NotImplementedError)` rather than through the reconciler subprocess, because `dispatch_one._update_one_apply_parent` swallows the exception'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the outbound oracle mechanism: name the DC API call used to read back the field value after an outbound pass (e.g., `transport.get_issue(key)` returning the updated summary/description/label/etc.), the specific field and expected value being checked, and add this to the AC alongside the existing inbound oracle specification.
evidence: Plan text: 'THIS is the epic's unproven half and the reason this story exists: test_reconcile_pass.py has three live tests and NONE mutates a local ticket then asserts the change surfaces on the DC issue'

Plan text for inbound: 'The oracle for this is already FIXED and PROVEN ... It now matches by exact id via _jira_key_to_local_id(remote_key) AND asserts the binding store. EVIDENCE: CI run 30662366152'
No equivalent read-back mechanism is named for the outbound direction — no API call (e.g., transport.get_issue(key)), no field/value pair, no assertion form is specified
The plan's own framing emphasizes observable outcomes over process assertions throughout, making this omission incongruent with the rest of the specification
findings.finding: The plan names the outbound round-trip criterion as the 'unproven half' and the reason this story exists, but does not specify the ORACLE MECHANISM for verifying that a local edit actually landed on the DC issue — i.e., it does not say which DC API call reads back the field value to confirm the change, or what field/value pair the assertion checks. Without an explicit read-back step, an implementation could satisfy the criterion by asserting only that the reconciler subprocess exited cleanly, which is exactly the 'green-but-broken' pattern the plan warns against elsewhere. The inbound oracle is fully specified (match by local id via `_jira_key_to_local_id`, assert binding store, CI run 30662366152 cited as evidence). The outbound oracle has no equivalent specification.
findings.location: AC: '[operator-attested] a local edit appears on the DC issue after an outbound pass' / section 'The DC-side mutation suite' / outbound list
scenarios: A test calls the reconciler on a locally-edited ticket, the subprocess exits 0, and the test asserts exit code == 0 — the DC issue is never read back, the test passes, but the mutation was silently dropped or mis-routed

The outbound differ computes zero mutations due to a stale prev_snapshot (the exact failure mode the scrub section explains) and the test passes because no exception escaped, matching the 'green-but-broken' pattern
findings.suggested_fix: After the outbound reconciler pass, call `transport.get_issue(remote_key)` (or equivalent on `JiraDataCenterTransport`) for the mutated issue and assert the specific field value matches the local edit — e.g., if the local title was edited to a test-unique string, assert `issue['fields']['summary'] == expected_summary`. This mirrors how the inbound oracle asserts the binding store and local id, giving both directions a symmetric, falsifiable check.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the citation `binding_store.py:113` to the actual location that documents binding-driven remote write semantics (e.g. the BindingStore class or the location where `jira_key` bindings gate outbound writes), or remove the line citation and state the design rationale without a false code reference.
evidence: Plan text: 'only BINDINGS drive remote writes — binding_store.py:113'

Actual binding_store.py:112-115: '# Bug 1e08-1a35-0267-4ca6 — binding lifecycle (GC) defaults. These are the / # reconciler's only int-valued binding env vars; parsed defensively below so a / # typo'd ops value degrades to the default rather than aborting the pass. / _DEFAULT_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE = 3'
This is about the absence-retire grace period env var, not about bindings driving remote writes
findings.finding: The plan cites `binding_store.py:113` to ground the claim that 'only BINDINGS drive remote writes' (used to justify why a whole-tree Jira key scan would always fail and must not be required). Line 113 in binding_store.py is actually the start of a comment about lifecycle int env var defaults (_DEFAULT_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE, line 115), with no content about bindings driving remote writes. The citation points to the wrong location and the claim is therefore unbacked by the cited evidence.
findings.location: The copy must be SCRUBBED section / AC: 'NOT "the copied store holds no production Jira key reference"' / citation 'binding_store.py:113'
scenarios: An implementer reading the plan to verify the scrub justification checks binding_store.py:113 and finds env var parsing code, not the design contract the plan claims to cite — leaving the scrub's rationale ungrounded

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define 'writes nothing' precisely (e.g., 'dry-run JSON plan array is empty: `jq -e ".plan | length == 0"`) and add it as the proving command for the idempotence AC, for both the post-inbound and post-outbound repeated passes.
evidence: 'writes nothing' appears without a definition of the observable
No jq, grep, or subprocess-output pattern is provided for the idempotence check
Earlier ACs specify dry-run JSON as the observable for the scrub check but do not extend that specification to idempotence
findings.finding: The idempotence acceptance criterion — 'a repeated pass after each direction writes nothing' — is ambiguous on two dimensions: (1) 'writes nothing' is undefined (does it mean zero plan entries in dry-run JSON, zero mutations applied in live mode, or both?), and (2) no proving command is specified for either direction, so an executor cannot implement or verify the check.
findings.location: AC: 'a repeated pass after each direction writes nothing (idempotence)'
scenarios: Executor uses a live-mode pass and checks only for exceptions, missing actual mutation replay

Executor uses dry-run but asserts on the prose 'OK: dry-run computed 0 mutations' line on stderr instead of the JSON plan array, which is an unreliable target per the plan's own note about stdout/stderr separation
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the AC line with: 'A repeated `--mode dry-run` pass immediately after each direction emits a JSON envelope whose `plan` array has length 0, asserted via `jq -e ".plan | length == 0"` on stdout.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a concrete proving command for full pagination recovery, e.g., 'count of issues in the local store matching the seeded keys equals `2 * observed_page_size + 1`, asserted via a deterministic script against the local ticket store.'
evidence: 'Assert the seeded issue count is FULLY recovered' — no jq, grep, or count-comparison command is given
Earlier dry-run JSON assertions are well-specified, making the absence of a proving command here conspicuous
findings.finding: The pagination 'fully recovered' assertion has no proving command. The AC states 'the suite seeds at least 2 * observed + 1 issues … Assert the seeded issue count is FULLY recovered' but provides no concrete command (e.g., a count of locally stored issues matching the seeded DC issues) to verify full recovery.
findings.location: AC: '…the suite seeds at least 2 * observed + 1 issues IN THE HARNESS so at least three pages are required … assert the seeded issue count is FULLY recovered'
scenarios: Executor checks only that the reconciler exits zero, not that the seeded count equals the recovered count
Silent truncation at the page boundary passes an exception-free check

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the exact assertion for 'zero unhandled exceptions': e.g., 'stderr contains no line matching `^(Traceback|.*Error:|.*Exception:)` AND exit code is 0', or reference the structured log field that records unhandled exceptions.
evidence: 'asserted on the reconciler subprocess streams' — no pattern specified
The plan carefully specifies stdout vs. stderr separation for the dry-run JSON but gives no equivalent for exception detection
findings.finding: 'Zero unhandled exceptions, asserted on the reconciler subprocess streams' names the target (subprocess streams) but provides no grep pattern, exit-code check, or parse protocol. An executor cannot implement a deterministic assertion from this description alone.
findings.location: AC: 'zero unhandled exceptions, asserted on the reconciler subprocess streams'
scenarios: Executor checks only exit code 0, missing exceptions that are caught and logged at WARNING level
Executor greps stderr for 'Exception' but misses 'Error' subclasses, or vice versa

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a concrete proving command for the base_url file-content check, e.g., `grep -rE 'base_url\s*=' <working_repo_config_dir> | grep -v <harness_url_pattern>` exits non-zero (no matches), and define what 'Jira host string' means (the specific domain or IP of the production instance).
evidence: 'every config file … that sets base_url sets it to the harness container URL' — no grep or find command specified
'no other Jira host string appears' — 'Jira host string' is undefined; an executor cannot know whether to grep for the domain, an IP, a URL prefix, or all three
findings.finding: The live-Jira-untouched assertion ('every config file in the working repo that sets base_url sets it to the harness container URL, and no other Jira host string appears in any config file there') is stated as a FILE-CONTENT check but no proving command is given — no grep invocation, no file path pattern, and no definition of 'Jira host string' (what regex? which config file extensions?).
findings.location: AC: 'this project's live Jira is untouched, asserted as a FILE-CONTENT check'
scenarios: Executor writes a grep for 'atlassian.net' but the real instance uses a custom domain, leaving the assertion vacuously passing
No command is specified so the check is implemented as a manual inspection, which is not deterministic

findings.finding: The issue-seeding mechanism for the pagination volume test is unspecified — the plan says 'seed at least 2 * observed + 1 issues IN THE HARNESS' but names no method (transport.create_issue? direct REST POST? pytest fixture factory?). Additionally, 'assert the seeded issue count is fully recovered' has no proving command (count of local tickets after inbound pass? a specific log line?).
findings.location: 'volume — and note WHAT drives it' section — 'seed at least `2 * observed + 1` issues' and 'assert the seeded issue count is fully recovered'
findings.suggested_fix: State: 'Seed via `transport.create_issue` in a pytest fixture; after the inbound pass assert `recovered_count == seed_count` where `recovered_count` is the number of newly-created tickets in the local store matching the seeded issue keys.'

findings.finding: The pagination test setup (seed 2*observed+1 issues) is correct, but the plan specifies NO assertion that ALL seeded issues actually appear in the local store after the inbound pass. Without an explicit count or membership assertion, a buggy paginator that truncates at page 1 would go undetected: the suite asserts individual round-trips for the mutations it explicitly creates, but those mutations can be placed on page 1, leaving pages 2+ silently unfetched and unverified.
findings.location: AC: 'the suite seeds at least 2 * observed + 1 issues IN THE HARNESS so at least three pages are required'; section 'volume — and note WHAT drives it'
findings.suggested_fix: After the inbound pass, assert `len(local_store.list_tickets()) >= 2 * observed_page_size + 1` (or assert that every seeded issue key appears in the local store). This is the only observable that proves pagination was exercised end-to-end rather than just set up.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a subsection or bullet in the Approach (under Isolation or Scope) that describes how the file-content base_url check is implemented: which config files exist in the working repo after store-copy and fixture setup, how the scan is run, and where the assertion lives.
evidence: AC text: 'every config file in the working repo that sets `base_url` sets it to the harness container URL, and no other Jira host string appears in any config file there'
Approach section enumerates four isolation layers; none is a config-file content scan

Scope: '.github/workflows/external-integration.yml — the jira-dc-harness job gains the store-copy step and the isolation assertions' — 'isolation assertions' is the only phrase that could encompass this, but it is not specific enough to confirm coverage
ABSENCE: no description in the Approach of how config files are generated, validated, or scanned in the working repo
findings.finding: The AC 'this project's live Jira is untouched, asserted as a FILE-CONTENT check rather than as "never resolves a non-harness base URL"... every config file in the working repo that sets `base_url` sets it to the harness container URL, and no other Jira host string appears in any config file there' specifies a concrete test mechanism (scan all config files in the working repo for base_url values and reject any non-harness host string). This mechanism appears nowhere in the Approach section or the Scope section. The Approach describes four isolation layers (no remote, REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off, no Cloud credentials, git-remote assertion) without mentioning a config-file content scan. The Scope lists the workflow and the test directory but does not describe where or how this check is implemented. The AC is an orphan: it specifies real implementation work with no corresponding body coverage.
findings.location: AC 'this project's live Jira is untouched, asserted as a FILE-CONTENT check...' vs. Approach section 'Isolation is the first requirement' and Scope section
scenarios: Implementer writes the four explicitly described isolation assertions and considers the isolation AC block complete, missing the file-content check entirely.

The file-content check is added ad-hoc without design consideration (e.g., which config files exist in the working repo after the store copy and fixture setup), leading to a brittle or incomplete scan.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the derivation of the `< 10` UPDATE threshold (e.g., 'derived by running dry-run on a known-clean copy and rounding up to the next power of two') and add a protocol for re-baselining it when the store grows.
evidence: 'fewer than 10 outbound UPDATE mutations' — no source for the number 10 is stated
The plan explicitly notes prev_snapshot.json absence causes spurious outbound UPDATEs, but gives no protocol for deriving the expected baseline count from store size or field-history depth
findings.finding: The `< 10` outbound UPDATE mutation threshold in the dry-run assertion has no stated derivation or method for recalibration. If the real ticket store grows (more tickets with field history), a future executor cannot determine whether a count of, say, 12 is a scrub failure or a legitimate store-growth effect, making the assertion unmaintainable and potentially a false-negative gate.
findings.location: AC: 'the first pass plans EXACTLY ZERO deletion mutations AND fewer than 10 outbound UPDATE mutations'
scenarios: Ticket store grows; the real baseline exceeds 10; the assertion fails on a correctly scrubbed store
A future executor cannot distinguish a scrub failure from store growth
findings.suggested_fix: Add a comment in the AC: 'Baseline measured by running dry-run on a freshly scrubbed copy with no prev_snapshot.json; current observed value is N; threshold is ceil(N * 1.5) rounded up to nearest 5, reassessed whenever the ticket store is retargeted.'

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).

AC item "this project's live Jira is untouched, asserted as a FILE-CONTENT check rather t" cites operational evidence (live_run) that lives outside the codebase but is not tagged [operator-attested]; prefix the checkbox text with [operator-attested] so the completion verifier accepts a recorded attestation instead of failing to find code proof.
findings.finding: Acceptance-criteria / definition-of-done quality issues.
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.finding: The outbound `set parent` mutation in the comprehensive suite conflates two structurally different cases without specifying how each is exercised: (a) the epic/non-subtask case, which raises `NotImplementedError` and must be asserted directly against the transport; and (b) the sub-task case, which actually WORKS and should go through the reconciler — but requires a sub-task to exist as a harness prerequisite, and the plan provides no setup instruction for creating one. As written, an implementer testing 'set parent' only via the NotImplementedError direct-transport assertion will leave the working sub-task code path exercised nowhere in this suite.
findings.location: DC mutation suite section — outbound mutations bullet: 'set parent; clear parent' and 'set_parent's epic case is expected to raise NotImplementedError ... asserted directly against the transport'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a note under the outbound 'set parent' bullet: 'The sub-task variant (the path that succeeds) is exercised by creating a Task as a sub-task of another issue in the harness before the outbound pass, then asserting via transport.set_parent directly or through the reconciler that the parent field is written. This is a separate assertion from the NotImplementedError check, which covers only the non-subtask (epic) branch.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Merge ACs 5 and 6 into a single criterion that states both the positive requirement (glob-based assertion, zero survivors) and the negative scoping (do NOT assert on production key references in ticket event files), eliminating the duplicate verifiable requirement.
evidence: AC 5: 'the scrub matches `.bridge_state*` as a GLOB and a test asserts ZERO binding or snapshot artifacts survive anywhere in the copied tree — derived by enumerating the tree, not from a hardcoded list'
AC 6: 'a test asserts the `.bridge_state*` scrub is COMPLETE — nothing matching `.bridge_state*` survives anywhere under the copied tracker dir, so a partially-scrubbed tree fails the job'
The only difference is AC 6 adds a 'NOT' clause about production key references, which is a scoping clarification, not a distinct verifiable requirement
findings.finding: ACs 5 and 6 both require the same test: that nothing matching the glob `.bridge_state*` survives anywhere in the copied tracker directory after scrubbing. AC 5 states: 'the scrub matches `.bridge_state*` as a GLOB and a test asserts ZERO binding or snapshot artifacts survive anywhere in the copied tree.' AC 6 states: 'a test asserts the `.bridge_state*` scrub is COMPLETE — nothing matching `.bridge_state*` survives anywhere under the copied tracker dir.' The positive requirement (a test that the glob finds nothing) is stated twice. AC 6 adds a negative clarification (do NOT assert on production key references) that is additive, but the core verifiable requirement is duplicated, creating two pass/fail gates that measure the same thing.
findings.location: AC 5 ('the scrub matches `.bridge_state*` as a GLOB...') and AC 6 ('a test asserts the `.bridge_state*` scrub is COMPLETE...')
scenarios: An implementer writes one test satisfying both ACs, then a reviewer marks AC 5 green and AC 6 green — no harm done but the redundancy adds review overhead.
If the two ACs are ever assigned to different sub-tasks, two implementers write the same test, creating a duplicate in the test suite.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the hardcoded `< 10` UPDATE threshold with a self-calibrating baseline: run a dry-run pass on a freshly-scrubbed store with NO seeded mutations, record the baseline UPDATE count, then assert that the post-mutation pass count equals baseline + expected-mutations — or at minimum, store the threshold in a named constant with a comment explaining how to re-derive it.
evidence: The threshold `< 10` is tied to the current state of this project's ticket store, which is a living dataset that changes with every sprint.
The plan gives no mechanism to update the threshold automatically or derive it from a baseline, so any store growth that pushes legitimate baseline UPDATEs above 9 will require a manual plan/AC edit.
findings.finding: The `< 10 outbound UPDATE mutations` threshold is hardcoded in the AC's jq assertion and will need to change as the real ticket store content evolves, but no mechanism is specified to make it configurable or self-calibrating — it will silently become a flaky gate as the store grows.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria — the dry-run assertion block: `jq -e '[.plan[] | select(.direction == "outbound" and .action == "update")] | length < 10'`
scenarios: Ticket store grows past ~10 baseline outbound drift items; the assertion starts failing on every CI run with no indication of whether it's a real scrub failure or simply a stale threshold.
A reviewer updating the threshold after store growth inadvertently relaxes the gate that was supposed to catch a bad `prev_snapshot.json` scrub.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify a wall-clock timeout for the reconciler subprocess call (e.g., `subprocess.run(..., timeout=300)`) and assert that a `TimeoutExpired` exception is surfaced as a test failure with a diagnostic message, not swallowed or treated as a passing no-output run.
evidence: The plan specifies asserting on subprocess stdout/stderr streams but does not specify a timeout for the subprocess call itself.
The DC harness is a Docker container whose availability is not guaranteed for the full duration of the test suite; a mid-pass container failure would leave the subprocess waiting on a socket read.
No circuit-breaker or timeout wrapper is mentioned anywhere in the plan.
findings.finding: The reconciler subprocess invocation has no specified timeout; a deadlocked or hung subprocess (e.g., the DC harness container stops responding mid-pass) would block the CI job indefinitely until the global runner wall-clock limit fires, making the failure mode opaque and the CI slot unavailable for that duration.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria — `zero unhandled exceptions, asserted on the reconciler subprocess streams`
scenarios: The Docker container OOMs or is killed by the CI runner mid-reconciliation pass; the subprocess blocks on `stdout.read()` until the global 6-hour GitHub Actions limit.
A pagination loop hits a server error that returns a non-empty but invalid page, causing the fetcher to loop indefinitely.
findings.suggested_fix: subprocess.run([...], timeout=300, capture_output=True, check=False) with an explicit assert on returncode and a timeout catch that re-raises as a named test failure.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add explicit error handling for the `git fetch origin tickets` step: check its exit code immediately and emit a human-readable diagnostic (e.g., 'FATAL: could not fetch orphan tickets branch — does it exist?') before any subsequent step runs, so a missing branch is the first error a maintainer sees.
evidence: The plan states the fetch is mandatory: 'The job must explicitly `git fetch origin tickets` in the SOURCE checkout', but specifies no fallback or failure message if it produces a non-zero exit.

A missing or renamed `tickets` branch would propagate silently through the `git archive FETCH_HEAD` step (which would fail with 'unknown revision'), and subsequent isolation assertions would fail for the wrong reason.
No CI step name or `|| echo` diagnostic is specified for this fetch.
findings.finding: The `git fetch origin tickets` step — required to materialise the orphan branch — has no error-handling or diagnostic path specified: if the `tickets` branch does not exist, has been renamed, or the fetch fails for any reason, all subsequent steps fail with confusing errors about `FETCH_HEAD` rather than a clear diagnostic pointing at the fetch step.
findings.location: Approach section — `git fetch origin tickets` / `git archive FETCH_HEAD | tar -x -C <fresh repo>`
scenarios: The `tickets` orphan branch is retargeted or renamed as part of a store migration; CI starts failing with a cryptic `fatal: ambiguous argument 'FETCH_HEAD'` error in the scrub step rather than a clear 'could not fetch tickets branch' message.
A shallow checkout configuration in a future workflow change prevents the fetch from completing.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reframe the sequencing criterion as a durable artifact requirement, e.g., 'the thin-slice CI run ID is recorded in the ticket before the comprehensive suite PR is opened', so it is verifiable at acceptance time as a concrete attestation rather than a past process event.
evidence: Under F1(c): 'a durable end-state, not a one-time transition (litmus: could it be false before this work and true only because of it?)'
Once the full suite is merged, the thin-slice CI run is in the past and the AC is trivially vacuous
findings.finding: The sequencing acceptance criterion ('the thin vertical slice … is green in CI BEFORE the comprehensive mutation suite lands') is a one-time process gate, not a durable end-state. Once the comprehensive suite is merged, this criterion can never be false again — it describes a transition event, not a persistent property of the codebase.
findings.location: AC: 'the thin vertical slice (fetch + scrub + isolation + one inbound and one outbound round-trip) is green in CI BEFORE the comprehensive mutation suite lands'
scenarios: At close of J11, the AC is considered met because it was true at some point during development, even if the thin slice was never re-run or was later broken by a commit in the same PR
A reviewer cannot verify a past CI state from the final merged commit
findings.suggested_fix: Record the thin-slice CI run ID as a ticket comment before the comprehensive suite PR is opened; close the criterion on that recorded run ID, not on a re-evaluable code state.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an entry to AGENTS.md (or a new ADR) recording: (a) rebar auto-commits and auto-pushes to `sync.remote`, (b) live tests therefore require a no-remote working repo as the primary isolation, and (c) the orphan-branch materialisation pattern is mandatory — not a convenience.
evidence: The plan introduces a new pattern: `git init` a fresh repo, copy tree from an orphan branch via `git archive`, never add a remote — this is a project-specific isolation contract not captured in any existing ADR.

The README.md specified covers the isolation contract, but READMEs in test directories are not the canonical location for architectural decisions and are routinely skipped when modifying CI workflows.
The plan explicitly flags that auto-push to `sync.remote` is the threat model, but this threat model and its mitigation are not recorded at the project level.
findings.finding: No ADR or AGENTS.md update is specified for the novel architectural decision of materialising the orphan `tickets` branch into a no-remote repo as the live-test isolation primitive — a future maintainer changing the CI job without understanding the auto-push risk will not find any canonical design record explaining why the no-remote constraint is mandatory.
findings.location: Scope section — `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` and `tests/external/live_jira_dc/README.md`
scenarios: A future CI refactor replaces `git init` + copy with `actions/checkout` + sparse-checkout of the tickets branch, reintroducing the missing-remote gap without realising the safety property has been broken.
New contributor adds `git remote add origin ...` to debug a fetch issue, inadvertently re-enabling the push path.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the `git archive FETCH_HEAD | tar -x` materialization step with the repo's established ADR-0005-compliant mechanism — either `git fetch` + `git worktree add` (as `opcert_service/workspace.py:123-125` does for the identical orphan-branch/no-remote problem) or `git read-tree` + `git checkout-index` — and explicitly note that `git archive` is excluded by ADR 0005 §D1.
evidence: Plan: 'git archive FETCH_HEAD | tar -x -C <fresh repo>'
ADR 0005 §D1: 'git archive is lossy as an attestation basis: it drops .gitattributes export-ignore paths, applies export-subst, omits submodule contents, and emits Git-LFS pointer text'
opcert_service/workspace.py:123-125 uses `git fetch` + `git worktree add` to mount the tickets branch into a fresh repo — the identical operation, using the ADR-approved mechanism

The ticket store could contain files tagged export-ignore; if any ticket event file is ever export-ignored, the copy would silently omit it and produce a store that diverges from the real content, defeating the 'realistic volume' goal
findings.finding: The plan's proposed tree-materialization mechanism (`git archive FETCH_HEAD | tar -x -C <fresh repo>`) conflicts with the repo's own standing ADR 0005, which explicitly rejects `git archive` for authoritative tree materialization as 'lossy' (drops `.gitattributes export-ignore` paths, applies `export-subst`, emits LFS pointer text rather than file content). The repo already has an established, proven alternative for the identical task — `opcert_service/workspace.py` uses `git fetch` + `git worktree add` to mount an orphan `tickets` branch from a remote into a fresh repo with no push path. The plan proposes a discarded pattern without acknowledging the standing ADR or the existing prior art.
findings.location: Approach section → 'HOW the content is obtained' bullet; ADR 0005 (docs/adr/0005-snapshot-cache-architecture.md §D1); opcert_service/workspace.py:101-145
scenarios: A ticket event file tagged with `export-ignore` in `.gitattributes` is silently dropped from the copy, making the scanned count lower than the real store and re-introducing the empty-store problem the plan exists to solve
An `export-subst` attribute on any store file causes the copy to contain substituted text rather than committed bytes, producing a store that differs from what the real project actually has
findings.suggested_fix: In the 'HOW the content is obtained' bullet, replace the `git archive` step with: `git init <dest> && git -C <dest> fetch <source-repo-path> tickets && git -C <dest> worktree add <tracker-dir> FETCH_HEAD` (or equivalently, `git read-tree FETCH_HEAD` into a throwaway GIT_INDEX_FILE + `git checkout-index`). Add a note: 'git archive is excluded by ADR 0005 §D1 — it drops export-ignore files and applies export-subst, both of which would silently corrupt the copy.'

findings.finding: The subject plan's acceptance criteria require operator-attested proof that 'an issue created in DC appears in the local store after an inbound pass', but the prerequisite establishes that the only test asserting this (test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance) cannot pass because it matches on the raw Jira key against a lowercased local id and the ticket payload carries no raw Jira key. The subject plan does not reference or account for fixing this oracle defect, yet it lists the operator-attested inbound round-trip as an acceptance criterion and treats a passing live job as evidence of correctness. As written, the subject plan cannot satisfy that criterion because the oracle is broken per the prerequisite.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria: '[operator-attested] an issue created in DC appears in the local store after an inbound pass'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a scope item and AC to fix the provenance test assertion per the prerequisite: match by exact id using _jira_key_to_local_id(remote_key) and assert the binding store, before claiming the operator-attested inbound AC.

findings.finding: The subject plan requires operator-attested inbound round-trips including assignee mutations (assign, unassign in the inbound mutation suite) and asserts zero unhandled exceptions, but the prerequisite proves that DC inbound identity minting silently fails (ValueError swallowed) for every DC pass, causing assignee resolution to degrade silently. The subject plan does not reference or scope a fix for this defect, yet its mutation suite and correctness claims depend on the inbound path working correctly for assignee-related mutations.
findings.location: Mutation suite: 'assign; unassign' in inbound mutations; AC: 'every mutation in the suite above round-trips, each asserted individually'; AC: 'zero unhandled exceptions'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a scope item to fix the vendor-to-family-channel mapping in apply_inbound_records.py per the prerequisite, and add an AC asserting identity is successfully minted (not merely that no exception escaped) for inbound DC assignee mutations.

findings.finding: The plan asserts that get_issuelinks_map and get_comment_map 'take the default max_results=50 with no offset loop' and that J11 is gated on ticket 9263 fixing this — but the current codebase already has the fix: both methods route through _paged_search at transport.py:454-475, which advances by len(batch) and stops on an empty page. Ticket 9263 is still marked 'in_progress' at the ticket level, but its file_impact is already reflected in the code. The plan's stated gating premise is factually wrong.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria: 'This criterion is only meaningful once [rebar:9263-b404-cb6c-463f] and [rebar:deac-4f5a-856a-49bd] are fixed'
findings.suggested_fix: Update the gating criterion to note that both 9263 and deac are already fixed in the codebase (deac closed, 9263 in-progress but code present); the criterion can be simplified to 'assert the seeded issue count is fully recovered' without the prerequisite gating, since both pagination fixes are already in main.

findings.finding: The plan asserts that fetcher._iter_pages 'stops on a SHORT page while advancing by the REQUESTED size (measured: 20 of 250 issues recovered against a page-capping server)' and cites ticket deac-4f5a-856a-49bd as an unfixed prerequisite. However, deac is CLOSED and its fix is already in the current codebase: fetcher.py:280-380 shows _iter_pages terminates on an EMPTY page only and advances by len(page). test_fetcher_pagination_heldout.py exists in the repo confirming the fix.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria: 'This criterion is only meaningful once [rebar:9263-b404-cb6c-463f] and [rebar:deac-4f5a-856a-49bd] are fixed', and the volume bullet: 'fetcher._iter_pages stops on a SHORT page while advancing by the REQUESTED size'
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the stale description with: 'fetcher._iter_pages (fixed, deac closed) terminates on an EMPTY page and advances by len(page). Both deac and 9263 are already fixed in the current codebase; the pagination seeding step in J11 can proceed without additional prerequisite gates.'

findings.finding: The plan's pagination-seeding AC states 'This criterion is only meaningful once [rebar:9263-b404-cb6c-463f] and [rebar:deac-4f5a-856a-49bd] are fixed'. Ticket deac is CLOSED (fix confirmed merged). Ticket 9263 is listed as `in_progress` in the ticket store, but the code in transport.py already contains `_paged_search` (line 421) and both `get_issuelinks_map` (line 455) and `get_comment_map` (line 469) already route through it. The gating claim presents 9263 as an open blocker when the code changes it describes may already be present in the repo, which could mislead the implementer into waiting for a ticket that is effectively code-complete.
findings.location: AC: 'This criterion is only meaningful once [rebar:9263-b404-cb6c-463f] and [rebar:deac-4f5a-856a-49bd] are fixed'

findings.finding: The AC reads deletion count and outbound UPDATE count from 'the `--mode dry-run` JSON envelope on stdout', but the specific JSON key names to extract those counts are never stated. An executor must guess the schema to write the `jq` assertion.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria — 'the first pass plans EXACTLY ZERO deletion mutations AND fewer than 10 outbound UPDATE mutations, both read from the `--mode dry-run` JSON envelope on stdout'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a representative dry-run JSON envelope snippet to the plan (even a two-key example) and reference the keys in the AC: e.g., 'assert `jq -e ".summary.delete_count == 0"` and `jq -e ".summary.outbound_update_count < 10"`'.

findings.finding: The AC 'the first inbound pass plans EXACTLY ZERO deletion mutations, asserted numerically' does not specify where or how the deletion mutation count is observable — whether from reconciler stdout, a structured log field, a summary line with a known format, or some other artifact. Without this, an agent cannot write a deterministic numeric assertion.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria: 'the first inbound pass plans EXACTLY ZERO deletion mutations, asserted numerically'

findings.finding: The AC 'the copied store holds NO production Jira key reference before the first pass' does not define what constitutes a 'production Jira key reference' — the pattern (e.g. a regex like `[A-Z]+-[0-9]+`, or specifically this project's Jira project key prefix, or the presence of any non-empty `remote_id` field in bindings) is unspecified. An implementing agent cannot write this test without deciding an approach that may or may not match the intent.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria: 'a test asserts the copied store holds NO production Jira key reference before the first pass'
findings.suggested_fix: State the project's Jira key prefix (e.g. 'PROJ') explicitly and define the check as: `grep -rE '"remote_id"\s*:\s*"PROJ-[0-9]+"' <copied_tree>` returns no matches. This is narrower than a raw key regex (avoids harness keys) and targets the field that actually binds local tickets to remote issues.
